questionText: What does the idiom BURN THE MIDNIGHT OIL mean?
options: A) Work late into the night
explanation: Burn the midnight oil means to stay up late working or studying. It refers to working hard into the night.

questionText: What does the proverb A STITCH IN TIME SAVES NINE mean?
options: B) Fix problems early before they worsen
C) Nine stitches are better than one
explanation: A stitch in time saves nine means it is better to deal with problems immediately rather than letting them worsen.

questionText: What does the idiom BITE THE BULLET mean?
options: B) Endure a painful situation stoically
explanation: Bite the bullet means to endure a painful or difficult situation with courage. It originates from soldiers biting bullets during surgery.

questionText: What does the proverb EVERY CLOUD HAS A SILVER LINING mean?
options: A) Clouds are made of silver
C) Every bad situation has a positive side
D) Look for silver in storms
explanation: Every cloud has a silver lining means that even in difficult situations there are positive aspects to be found.

questionText: What does the idiom TURN OVER A NEW LEAF mean?
options: A) Change pages in a book
B) Start fresh with better behavior
explanation: Turn over a new leaf means to change one behavior or attitude for the better.

questionText: What does the proverb STRIKE WHILE THE IRON IS HOT mean?
options: C) Act at the right moment
explanation: Strike while the iron is hot means to act at the most favorable time, when conditions are right.

questionText: What does the idiom COST AN ARM AND A LEG mean?
explanation: Cost an arm and a leg means to be extremely expensive. It is used when something costs a lot of money.

questionText: What does the proverb LOOK BEFORE YOU LEAP mean?
explanation: Look before you leap means to think carefully about possible risks or consequences before taking action.

questionText: What does the idiom HIT THE NAIL ON THE HEAD mean?
explanation: Hit the nail on the head means to describe exactly what is causing a situation or problem.

questionText: What does the proverb ALL THAT GLITTERS IS NOT GOLD mean?
options: B) Not everything valuable looks valuable
D) Things are not always what they appear
explanation: All that glitters is not gold means things are not always what they appear - not everything attractive is actually valuable.

questionText: What does the idiom BREAK A LEG mean?
explanation: Break a leg is a way to say good luck especially to performers before they go on stage.

questionText: What does the proverb THE EARLY BIRD CATCHES THE WORM mean?
options: B) Worms are best in morning
C) Success comes to those who act early
explanation: The early bird catches the worm means that people who start early or act promptly will be more successful.

questionText: What does the idiom SPILL THE BEANS mean?
options: A) Have an accident with food
explanation: Spill the beans means to reveal secret or hidden information, often accidentally.

questionText: What does the proverb DONT COUNT YOUR CHICKENS BEFORE THEY HATCH mean?
options: C) Do not assume success before it happens
explanation: Do not count your chickens before they hatch means do not make plans based on something that has not happened yet.

questionText: What does the idiom UNDER THE WEATHER mean?
explanation: Under the weather means feeling slightly ill or unwell. It is used to describe minor sickness.

questionText: What does the proverb ACTIONS SPEAK LOUDER THAN WORDS mean?
options: B) What people do matters more than what they say
explanation: Actions speak louder than words means what someone does is more important and telling than what they say.

questionText: What does the idiom LET THE CAT OUT OF THE BAG mean?
explanation: Let the cat out of the bag means to accidentally reveal information that was supposed to be kept secret.

questionText: What does the proverb WHEN IN ROME DO AS THE ROMANS DO mean?
options: C) Follow local customs when visiting
explanation: When in Rome do as the Romans do means to follow the customs and behavior of people in whatever place you visit.

questionText: What does the idiom PULL SOMEONES LEG mean?
explanation: Pull someone leg means to joke with or tease someone in a light-hearted way.

questionText: What does the proverb DONT JUDGE A BOOK BY ITS COVER mean?
options: C) Do not judge by appearances alone
explanation: Do not judge a book by its cover means do not form an opinion about someone or something based only on appearances.

questionText: What does the idiom ONCE IN A BLUE MOON mean?
explanation: Once in a blue moon means very rarely or almost never. A blue moon is a rare occurrence.

questionText: What does the proverb NECESSITY IS THE MOTHER OF INVENTION mean?
options: B) Need drives people to create solutions
explanation: Necessity is the mother of invention means that difficult situations inspire creative solutions.

questionText: What does the idiom PIECE OF CAKE mean?
explanation: Piece of cake means something that is very easy to do. It suggests an effortless task.

questionText: What does the proverb HONESTY IS THE BEST POLICY mean?
options: B) Being truthful always leads to better outcomes
explanation: Honesty is the best policy means that it is always better to tell the truth even when it is difficult.

questionText: What does the idiom BACK TO THE DRAWING BOARD mean?
options: B) Start a project over from the beginning
explanation: Back to the drawing board means to start something again from the beginning because the current approach failed.

questionText: What does the proverb TWO WRONGS DONT MAKE A RIGHT mean?
options: B) Responding to wrongdoing with wrongdoing is not justified
explanation: Two wrongs do not make a right means that responding to a wrong action with another wrong action does not correct anything.

questionText: What does the idiom BITE OFF MORE THAN YOU CAN CHEW mean?
options: B) Take on more than one can handle
explanation: Bite off more than you can chew means to take on more responsibility or work than one can manage.

questionText: What does the proverb BIRDS OF A FEATHER FLOCK TOGETHER mean?
options: B) People of similar nature tend to associate together
explanation: Birds of a feather flock together means that people with similar interests and characters tend to spend time together.

questionText: What does the idiom THE BALL IS IN YOUR COURT mean?
options: B) It is your decision or responsibility now
explanation: The ball is in your court means it is now your responsibility to take action or make a decision.

questionText: What does the proverb PRACTICE MAKES PERFECT mean?
options: B) Repeated practice leads to improvement
explanation: Practice makes perfect means that consistent practice and repetition leads to mastery of a skill.

questionText: What does the idiom THROW IN THE TOWEL mean?
options: B) Give up or admit defeat
explanation: Throw in the towel means to admit defeat or give up on something. It comes from boxing where a trainer throws a towel to stop a fight.

questionText: What does the proverb SLOW AND STEADY WINS THE RACE mean?
options: B) Careful consistent work leads to success
explanation: Slow and steady wins the race means that being careful and consistent is better than rushing and making mistakes.

questionText: What does the idiom GET OUT OF HAND mean?
options: B) Lose control or become unmanageable
explanation: Get out of hand means to become out of control or unmanageable. Situations that get out of hand are difficult to manage.

questionText: What does the proverb UNITED WE STAND DIVIDED WE FALL mean?
options: B) Unity gives strength while division leads to weakness
explanation: United we stand divided we fall means that people are stronger when they work together than when they work separately.

questionText: What does the idiom BEAT AROUND THE BUSH mean?
explanation: Beat around the bush means to avoid talking about the main point or to approach a topic indirectly.

questionText: What does the proverb THE PEN IS MIGHTIER THAN THE SWORD mean?
options: B) Words and writing are more powerful than violence
explanation: The pen is mightier than the sword means that written communication and intellectual power are more effective than military force.

questionText: What does the idiom ON THE FENCE mean?
explanation: On the fence means unable to decide or having no strong opinion on an issue. A person on the fence is undecided.

questionText: What does the proverb IF IT AINT BROKE DONT FIX IT mean?
options: B) Do not try to change something that is working
explanation: If it aint broke do not fix it means do not try to change or improve something that already works well.

questionText: What does the idiom ADD FUEL TO THE FIRE mean?
options: B) Make a bad situation worse
explanation: Add fuel to the fire means to make an already difficult situation worse by doing or saying something to intensify it.

questionText: What does the proverb ROME WAS NOT BUILT IN A DAY mean?
options: B) Great things take time and effort
explanation: Rome was not built in a day means that important things take time to develop and one should not expect immediate results.

questionText: What does the idiom MISS THE BOAT mean?
explanation: Miss the boat means to miss an opportunity or to be too late to take advantage of something.

questionText: What does the proverb TOO MANY COOKS SPOIL THE BROTH mean?
options: B) Too many people involved in something can ruin it
explanation: Too many cooks spoil the broth means that having too many people involved in managing or doing something can make it go wrong.

questionText: What does the idiom KEEP YOUR CHIN UP mean?
options: B) Stay positive in difficult times
explanation: Keep your chin up means to remain cheerful and positive during difficult or sad times.

questionText: What does the proverb THE GRASS IS ALWAYS GREENER ON THE OTHER SIDE mean?
options: B) What others have always seems better than what we have
explanation: The grass is always greener on the other side means people tend to think others have it better than they do.

questionText: What does the idiom HIT THE SACK mean?
explanation: Hit the sack means to go to bed or to go to sleep. Sack is an informal word for bed.

questionText: What does the proverb KNOWLEDGE IS POWER mean?
options: B) Having information gives one an advantage
explanation: Knowledge is power means that having information and education gives a person an advantage and ability to succeed.

questionText: What does the idiom KILL TWO BIRDS WITH ONE STONE mean?
options: B) Accomplish two things with a single action
explanation: Kill two birds with one stone means to accomplish two tasks with a single action or effort.

questionText: What does the proverb WHERE THERE IS A WILL THERE IS A WAY mean?
options: B) Determination leads to finding solutions
explanation: Where there is a will there is a way means if you are determined to do something you will find a way to do it.

questionText: What does the idiom GET A TASTE OF YOUR OWN MEDICINE mean?
options: B) Experience the same treatment you give to others
explanation: Get a taste of your own medicine means to experience the same unpleasant treatment that you have given to others.

questionText: What does the proverb CHARITY BEGINS AT HOME mean?
options: B) Be kind to family before helping strangers
explanation: Charity begins at home means that people should take care of family members and those close to them before helping others.
